games.title: Fallacy Noir
games.tagline: A rain-soaked detective story where every lie hides a broken argument.
description: It is 1947, the city never stops raining, and every witness in the precinct has a story that almost holds together. As a rookie detective with an unusually sharp ear for bad logic, you crack cases by catching the fallacies buried in testimony: the straw man, the false dilemma, the convenient appeal to authority.

Pin statements to your evidence board, connect contradictions with red string, and confront suspects when you can name exactly why their reasoning fails. Accuse the wrong person on a hunch and the case goes cold. By the last chapter you will hear a slippery slope coming from a block away.
features: 12 hand-written cases with over 40 fallacy types hidden in testimony
An evidence board where you link claims, contradictions and motives
Interrogations that branch on how precisely you name the flaw
A casebook that turns every solved fallacy into a quick reference card

games.title: Prompt Forge
games.tagline: Word your spells precisely, or your golem will take them literally.
description: Deep in a mountain forge lives Brom, an ancient golem who will build anything you ask for, exactly as you ask for it. Ask for "a sword" and you get a sword the size of a house. Ask him to "fix the bridge" and he may fix it permanently in place. Your job as the forge's new apprentice is to learn how to ask.

Each commission is a puzzle in clear instructions: give context, set constraints, show examples, and break big jobs into steps. Villagers bring stranger requests as the seasons pass, and Brom's quirks mirror the real habits of modern AI models, so the craft you learn here carries straight over to the tools on your desk.
features: 60+ commissions solved by writing instructions, not by clicking
Brom reacts to vague wording, missing context and conflicting goals
Unlock rune techniques modeled on real prompting patterns
A sandbox forge to experiment with your own requests

games.title: Signal & Noise
games.tagline: Keep the lighthouse burning by finding the truth hidden in the data.
description: You are the last keeper of a lighthouse on the edge of an ocean made of numbers. Ships only make it home if you can turn raw readings into a picture they can trust. Pick the right chart, pick the right scale, and the storm opens up to show a safe channel. Pick the wrong ones and the fleet sails straight onto the rocks.

Between storms, rival keepers send out charts of their own, some honest and some bent: truncated axes, cherry-picked ranges, averages hiding outliers. Expose the misleading ones before the harbor believes them. Every run brings new datasets, new weather and new ways for numbers to lie.
features: Procedural datasets and storms, so no two voyages are alike
Build charts from a deck of chart types, scales and encodings
Spot and debunk misleading graphs from rival lighthouses
Meta-progression that unlocks new lenses, filters and statistics

games.title: Firewall Farm
games.tagline: A cozy farming sim where the pests are phishing and the crops are your data.
description: Grandma left you the old farm in Byte Hollow, and with it the village's entire network. Your fields grow data, your barn is a server rack, and every season brings new pests: phishing moths that mimic friendly letters, ransomware crows that lock up the silo, and password weeds that spread wherever someone reused "harvest123".

Plant strong fences, rotate your keys like crops, teach villagers to check who really sent that letter, and decide what the farm actually needs to keep. It is a slow, cozy game with real security thinking underneath: least privilege, backups, patching and privacy by design, all learned one harvest at a time.
features: Four seasons of threats modeled on real attack patterns
Villagers with their own security habits you can help improve
Backups, patches and access rules that work like farm upkeep
A privacy almanac that decides which data the farm should never keep

games.title: The Negotiator's Table
games.tagline: Talk a floating city back from the brink, one conversation at a time.
description: The sky city of Aerith is held up by five guilds, and all five have stopped speaking to each other. As the city's newly appointed mediator, you sit down with miners, weavers, sky pilots, archivists and merchants, and try to find what each of them actually needs underneath what they are shouting about.

Conversations are played with cards: listen, reflect, reframe, name the emotion, propose a trade. Read the tells in each character's face, notice when pride is louder than interest, and build agreements that hold. Push too hard and a district loses power; get it right and whole storylines open up.
features: A card-driven dialogue system built on real mediation techniques
Characters with hidden interests you uncover by listening
Choices that ripple across the city and change later negotiations
Multiple endings shaped by trust rather than by force

games.title: Cloud Cartographer
games.tagline: Build a city in the sky that survives the traffic storms.
description: Your city floats on clouds, and so does everything it runs on. Lay out districts, route the flow of travelers across bridges and airways, and keep the lights on when a festival triples the crowd overnight. Every building is a service; every bridge is a dependency; every storm is a real failure mode.

Start with one sturdy tower and discover why it creaks under load. Split it into districts, add caches and queues, spread across islands so a single lightning strike cannot take everything down, and automate the crews that rebuild after each storm. It plays like a relaxing city builder until the traffic arrives.
features: Traffic surges, outages and storms modeled on real system failures
Services, caches, queues and load balancers as city buildings
Automation crews that deploy, monitor and recover on their own
A post-storm review screen that shows exactly what broke and why

games.title: Coin & Tide
games.tagline: Grow a tiny island economy across fifty years of storms and good seasons.
description: You inherit a small island, a leaky fishing boat and fifty years. Each turn is a season: decide what to spend, what to save, and what to plant for a harvest you may not see for a decade. Coin & Tide makes compounding visible, as a single sapling you planted early grows into the orchard that carries you through a bad storm late in life.

Traders offer loans with tempting terms, merchants sell insurance against storms that may never come, and a shiny new boat is always one season away. Inflation quietly raises the price of nets, diversification keeps one bad catch from sinking you, and the islanders you help early come back to help you later.
features: Fifty seasons of saving, investing and weathering storms
Compound growth you can literally watch grow as an orchard
Loans, insurance and inflation explained through island life
Random storms and booms that reward a diversified island

games.title: Expedition Zero
games.tagline: Lead six people across a frozen world where no plan survives the first storm.
description: A research crew of six, a supply sled, and eight hundred kilometers of ice between you and the only way home. You are not the strongest member of the team, or the best navigator. You are the one who has to decide. Expedition Zero is a survival game about leadership under uncertainty: who scouts, who rests, when to push on and when to wait out the storm.

Every crew member has skills, fears and a breaking point. Delegate well and the team outperforms any one of them; ignore someone's warning and you may lose more than supplies. Plans change daily, information is always incomplete, and the best leaders adapt without losing the trust they have built.
features: A six-person crew with personalities, trust and morale
Daily planning where every order trades one risk for another
Procedural weather and terrain that break even the best plans
A debrief after each expedition that reviews your key calls

games.title: Neuron Garden
games.tagline: Grow a glowing neural network and teach it to see the world.
description: Neuron Garden turns machine learning into gardening. Plant layers of luminous neurons, connect them with vines, and feed your garden examples to learn from: pictures of birds, handwritten letters, the sounds of rain. Watch the connections brighten as it learns, and watch weeds of overfitting creep in when you water it too much with the same data.

Each greenhouse is a new problem, from sorting fruit to predicting the weather. Prune, rebalance and test your garden on examples it has never seen. It is calm, beautiful and surprisingly honest about how real models learn, fail and get better.
features: A living network you grow layer by layer, vine by vine
Training, validation and overfitting shown as a changing garden
Greenhouse challenges covering vision, sound and prediction
A zen mode with no goals, only growing

games.title: Launch Day
games.tagline: Ship the product before scope creep eats the whole team.
description: You have one quarter, a small team, and a product idea that everyone loves in a different way. Launch Day is a roguelite about building the right thing: interview users to find the real problem, sketch and test designs, cut features ruthlessly, and ship before the deadline arrives.

Scope creep is a monster that grows every time you say "sure, we can add that". Stakeholders pull the roadmap in different directions, prototypes reveal what users actually do, and every sprint is a fresh draft of cards you play to plan the week. Each run is a new product, a new market and a new chance to get launch day right.
features: A deckbuilder where cards are research, design and delivery moves
User interviews that reveal the problem behind the request
Scope creep, stakeholders and deadlines as escalating threats
Procedural products and markets for endless runs

games.title: Chess Defense
games.tagline: Hold your back row against endless waves of enemy chess pieces.
description: Chess Defense turns the oldest strategy game into a siege. Enemy pieces march down the board in waves, each moving by its own chess rules, and you place and move your defenders to hold the back row for as long as you can.

Every wave asks the same questions a good chess player asks: which threat matters most, which trade is worth it, and which move sets up the next three. The browser prototype is being rebuilt into a full game with campaigns, new piece types and a daily challenge board.
features: Wave-based defense where every enemy follows real chess movement
Campaign boards with new terrain and piece types
A daily challenge board shared by every player
Replays that show where your defense first began to crack

games.title: Hypercube Tic-Tac-Toe
description: You know how to win tic-tac-toe on a 3x3 grid. Now play it on a cube, then on a tesseract, then in twelve dimensions, where lines of three run in directions your intuition has never seen.

Hypercube Tic-Tac-Toe trains the skill of holding a complex space in your head: projecting it, slicing it, and spotting patterns that only appear from the right angle. The full version adds new ways to visualize higher dimensions, puzzle modes and online matches against friends.
features: Boards from 2 up to 12 dimensions
Several projection views to rotate and slice the hypercube
Puzzle mode with handcrafted win-in-N challenges
An AI opponent that adapts to your level

games.title: Rupture Pattern System
games.tagline: Break 12 AI guardians by finding the fixed logic behind their moves.
description: Twelve AI guardians protect the system core, and each one plays Rock-Paper-Scissors by a fixed rule. Some mirror you, some counter your last move, some cycle, and the last ones hide their patterns inside patterns. Find the rule and win nine rounds out of ten to break through.

Rupture Pattern System is a game about noticing: forming a hypothesis, testing it cheaply, and throwing it away the moment the evidence disagrees. The full release expands the ladder with new guardians, a story campaign inside the system and a mode for designing guardians of your own.
features: A ladder of 12 guardians, each with its own hidden rule
Hypothesis tools to log, test and discard pattern guesses
A cyberpunk story campaign inside the system
A guardian editor for designing and sharing your own

books.title: The Machine That Guessed
books.subtitle: How AI really works, told through the mistakes it makes
books.overview: Every AI system you use is, at heart, a very fast guesser. This book follows a curious teenager and her grandmother's old chess computer as they poke, prod and occasionally break the AI tools around them. Each chapter starts with a strange AI failure and works backward to the idea that explains it, so by the end you can predict when an AI will shine, when it will bluff, and what questions to ask before trusting it.
concepts: Where AI is reliable and where it is not

books.title: From Notebook to Nightshift
books.subtitle: The journey of one model from a laptop experiment to a system millions depend on
books.overview: A promising model works beautifully in a notebook on Friday and falls over in production on Monday. This book tells the story of that model's first year in the real world: messy data pipelines, drifting inputs, silent failures at 3 a.m. and the engineers who learn to catch them. Along the way you learn the craft that turns a clever experiment into a dependable service.

books.title: Say What You Mean
books.subtitle: The art of talking to machines that take you literally
books.overview: A genie grants wishes exactly as spoken, and every wish goes wrong in a new way. In this playful book, a young apprentice learns to phrase requests to a literal-minded genie, and each lesson maps directly onto how to write prompts for today's AI models. You will learn to give context, set constraints, show examples and break big problems into steps, and you will laugh at the genie's disasters along the way.

books.title: The Detective in Your Head
books.subtitle: Solving everyday mysteries with evidence, logic and a little doubt
books.overview: Every day you are handed claims dressed as facts: headlines, ads, arguments, rumors. This book turns you into a detective of ideas. Through short cases, from a suspicious miracle diet to a village convinced a ghost stole the bread, you learn to question sources, weigh evidence, spot fallacies and change your mind when the facts demand it.

books.title: Untangle
books.subtitle: A field guide to breaking big, messy problems into small solvable ones
books.overview: Big problems look impossible because we see them as one giant knot. Untangle follows an engineer, a chef and a city planner as each faces a crisis that seems hopeless, and shows how they pull the knot apart: define the real problem, split it into pieces, test assumptions, and find the root cause instead of the loudest symptom.

books.title: Numbers Have Feelings Too
books.subtitle: How to read, question and trust the data that shapes your life
books.overview: Numbers don't lie, but they can be framed, cropped, averaged and cherry-picked until they say almost anything. This warm and funny book introduces a cast of personified numbers, from the anxious Outlier to the smug Average, to show how data is collected, summarized and sometimes abused. You will come away able to read a statistic and ask the right questions before believing it.

books.title: The Question Behind the Spreadsheet
books.subtitle: Turning rows of data into decisions people actually make
books.overview: A small bakery is losing money and nobody knows why. Its owner hands a nervous new analyst a messy spreadsheet and one week. This story-driven book follows that week from cleaning the data to exploring it, testing ideas and presenting a finding the owner can act on. It teaches the analytics workflow as a detective story with flour on its hands.

books.title: Drawing the Invisible
books.subtitle: How great charts reveal what numbers alone hide
books.overview: Florence Nightingale changed how hospitals worked with one diagram. This book tells the stories behind famous charts, from cholera maps to climate stripes, and uses them to teach the principles of good visual design. Learn to choose the right chart, use color with purpose, remove clutter and design a graphic that makes the right point impossible to miss.

books.title: The Castle Has a Thousand Doors
books.subtitle: Defending organizations when attackers need only one way in
books.overview: A medieval castle hires a new keeper of the gates, and discovers the walls matter far less than the servants who leave side doors open. Told as a castle chronicle that mirrors modern organizations, this book explains threats, defenses, risk and people-first security. It shows how security leaders decide what to protect first when they cannot protect everything.

books.title: The Glass House
books.subtitle: Living, building and leading in a world that remembers everything
books.overview: Imagine living in a house with glass walls where every neighbor keeps notes. That is roughly how our data lives today. This book follows a young product team building an app that people love, and the day they realize how much they know about their users. It explains privacy principles, regulations and design choices that respect people while still building great products.

books.title: Water Finds a Way
books.subtitle: Thriving when the plan, the job and the world keep changing
books.overview: A river never argues with a rock; it goes around, under or through. This book gathers stories of people who faced sudden change, from a chef whose restaurant closed overnight to a pilot improvising a landing, and draws out the habits that let them adapt instead of break. You will learn to loosen your grip on the old plan, learn fast and treat change as information.

books.title: The Weather Inside
books.subtitle: Understanding the storms and sunshine in yourself and others
books.overview: Emotions are like weather: they pass through, they can be forecast, and they shape every plan we make. Using this simple metaphor, the book teaches you to notice your own inner weather, read the forecast in other people, and respond instead of react. Short stories from offices, families and friendships show emotional intelligence as a skill you can practice every day.

books.title: The Last to Eat
books.subtitle: What real leaders do when nobody is watching
books.overview: Leadership is not a title; it is a set of choices, often small and often invisible. This book follows a reluctant new team lead through her first year, from the first awkward one-on-one to the crisis that tests everyone's trust. It covers vision, delegation, feedback and accountability through a story you will recognize from your own workplace.

books.title: The Orchestra Without a Conductor
books.subtitle: How great teams listen, coordinate and create together
books.overview: What happens when an orchestra loses its conductor on the night of the big concert? This lively book follows the musicians as they figure out how to play together without anyone waving a baton. Their story reveals the ingredients of great teamwork: shared goals, clear roles, psychological safety and the courage to speak up when something sounds wrong.

books.title: The Idea Kitchen
books.subtitle: Recipes for thinking up things that did not exist yesterday
books.overview: Creativity is less lightning bolt and more cooking: you combine ingredients, taste, adjust and try again. The Idea Kitchen serves up techniques as recipes, from mixing unrelated ideas to flipping assumptions upside down, with stories of inventors, artists and ordinary people who cooked up something new. Every chapter ends with a quick exercise you can do in ten minutes.

books.title: Castles in the Sky
books.subtitle: What the cloud really is, and how the internet stays up
books.overview: The cloud is not fluffy. It is millions of machines in giant buildings, humming day and night. This book takes you on a tour of an imaginary sky kingdom built on those machines, showing how data centers, networks, storage and virtual servers fit together, and why smart architects plan for things to fail.

books.title: Blueprints for Invisible Buildings
books.subtitle: Designing software that can grow without collapsing
books.overview: Software has architecture just like cities do, only you cannot see it until the traffic jams start. This book uses the story of a small town growing into a metropolis to explain how software systems are structured, from single buildings to districts connected by roads. You will learn the trade-offs architects weigh and why the simplest design that works is usually the best one.

books.title: The Night the Deploy Broke
books.subtitle: How teams ship faster by breaking down walls
books.overview: At 2 a.m. the website is down, developers blame operations, and operations blames developers. This gripping story follows one company's worst night and the months of change that follow, as the team learns to automate, measure and share responsibility. It explains the practices behind DevOps and shows why culture matters as much as tools.

books.title: One Click, Ten Journeys
books.subtitle: Follow a single button press from screen to server and back
books.overview: When you click a button on a website, a tiny message sets off on an epic journey. This book follows that message as a character, through the browser, across the network, into the server, down to the database and back, meeting the technologies that live at each stop. It is the clearest map of the full stack you will ever read.
concepts: Front end: HTML, CSS and JavaScript

books.title: Build the Right Thing
books.subtitle: How product managers decide what gets made, and what never does
books.overview: Most failed products were built perfectly; they just solved the wrong problem. This book follows a first-time product manager as she learns to listen to users, say no to good ideas, and steer a team toward something people truly need. Filled with real stories of product wins and flops, it teaches the thinking behind great products.

books.title: Doors That Tell You How to Open Them
books.subtitle: Designing things people understand without instructions
books.overview: Ever pushed a door that said pull? That was a design failure, not yours. This book explores why some things are a joy to use and others make us feel stupid, starting with everyday objects and moving to apps and websites. You will learn how designers research, sketch, test and refine until the right action feels obvious.

books.title: The Bridge Must Open on Tuesday
books.subtitle: Delivering on time when everything tries to slow you down
books.overview: A town has promised its new bridge will open on Tuesday, and the project manager has just discovered the steel is late. This page-turner follows the project from kickoff to ribbon-cutting, showing how to plan, estimate, manage risks and keep people aligned. You will learn the tools of the trade and when to set them aside.

books.title: The Crowded Square
books.subtitle: Getting noticed, trusted and chosen online
books.overview: The internet is a town square with a billion people shouting at once. This book follows a tiny handmade candle shop trying to be heard, as it learns to find its audience, tell its story, choose its channels and measure what works. It covers the strategy behind modern marketing without the jargon.

books.title: The Librarian of Everything
books.subtitle: How search engines decide what you find, and how to be found
books.overview: Imagine a librarian who has read every page on the internet and must recommend the best one in half a second. This book explains how that librarian works: crawling, indexing, ranking and understanding what people really mean. Then it shows how to create pages the librarian loves, by being genuinely useful rather than tricking the system.

books.title: The Tree That Grew Coins
books.subtitle: Money, saving and investing, explained like a story
books.overview: Two siblings each inherit a small sapling and a handful of coins. One spends quickly, the other plants and waits. Over the years their paths show how saving, investing, debt and compound growth really work. This friendly book makes money concepts easy to understand and gives you practical habits for your own financial life.

books.title: Three Moves Ahead
books.subtitle: Thinking like a strategist in business and in life
books.overview: Chess players, generals and CEOs share a habit: they think about where the game is going, not only where it is. This book uses stories from history, sports and business to explain how strategists set goals, analyze the landscape, make choices and adapt their plans as the board changes.

books.title: The Bridge Between Two Villages
books.subtitle: Turning disagreements into agreements people keep
books.overview: Two villages have fought over the same river for a hundred years. When a young mediator is sent to make peace, she discovers that the fight was never really about water. This fable-like book teaches the tools of conflict resolution: active listening, separating people from problems, finding shared interests and crafting solutions both sides can own.

books.title: The Umbrella Paradox
books.subtitle: Deciding well when you cannot know what will happen
books.overview: Carry an umbrella every day and you look silly on sunny days; never carry one and one day you get soaked. This book explores how people and organizations live with uncertainty, from sailors to startups to hospitals. You will learn to identify risks, weigh likelihood against impact and choose the right amount of protection.

books.title: The Fork in the Fog
books.subtitle: Choosing well when there are too many options and too little information
books.overview: Some decisions are easy. The ones that matter rarely are: many options, conflicting goals, missing information and a clock that keeps ticking. Through stories of mountain rescues, medical dilemmas and business gambles, this book gives you practical tools to structure hard choices, avoid common thinking traps and make decisions you can stand behind.

books.title: The Endless Library Card
books.subtitle: How to keep learning for the rest of your life, and enjoy it
books.overview: School ends; learning shouldn't. This inspiring book shares the science of how we learn and the stories of people who picked up new skills at 30, 60 and even 90. You will discover techniques like spaced repetition and deliberate practice, and learn how to stay curious, build habits and make learning a joyful part of everyday life.
